Decision equivalence is robust to fitting strategy. The joint fit's AUC_inf runs a bit wider than PBPK (e.g. n=86: 5.80 vs 5.05) — the unstable extrapolation for slow flip-flop tablets, which is why AUC₀–t is the primary AUC endpoint. Fit: OFV ≈ 6093.6.

Result · IVIVC / identifiability

Release scale α is flat — in both fits

Fitted geometric-mean α (h) vs PBPK T50
T501233.54567
α · per-arm1.421.601.691.651.681.651.691.71
α · joint1.431.571.681.671.721.711.701.76
Where the formulation effect went (joint fit, gm)
T50147
α (h)1.431.721.76
CL (L/h)10.612.214.7
Vc (L)86130190

Joint IVIVC exponent slope = 0.10 (≈ flat). The release-rate signal is not identifiable from sparse 1-compartment data (flip-flop): it is absorbed into apparent CL and Vc, which rise with T50 instead of α. PopPK reproduces the BE decision, not the release mechanism.

Sensitivity 2 · within-subject variability

Low-variability (ER) vs high-variability (IR) CV

Endpoint · nER CVIR CV

CVw — ER: Cmax 12.2%, AUC 11.2% (FDA NDA 212595). IR bound: Cmax 23.7%, AUC 14.7%. Higher CV narrows the safe space ~0.4–0.5 h per side; type-I error stays ≤ 5%.

10

Sensitivity 3 · study size · and results index

Study size, and everything at a glance

Study size n

48 → 86

Joint safe space widens only ~0.1 h per side (1.95–4.10 → 1.85–4.25). A low-within-subject-CV signature — bigger trials barely help.

Reference

T50 3.0 h

All GMRs relative to the 3.0 h reference; 8 formulations swept 1–7 h; 24 paired subjects.

Absolute exposure

~3–4×

PBPK over-predicts vs clinic (Cmax 2.8 µg/mL). Shared offset → cancels in the ratio → no effect on the safe space.
